steps.title: Sun and cool nights
steps.body: Marlborough, at the north-east tip of New Zealand's South Island, has long, sunny days, high UV light and cold nights. That combination gives intensely aromatic Sauvignon with ripe tropical fruit and piercing acidity at the same time. Stony, free-draining soils in the Wairau Valley help.
steps.highlight: Sun by day, cold by night

steps.title: The style
steps.body: Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is explosive: passion fruit, gooseberry, grapefruit, cut grass and green pepper, with high acidity. Cloudy Bay's 1985 vintage made it famous worldwide. Today Sauvignon Blanc is about 60% of New Zealand's vineyards and over 80% of its exports.

steps.prompt: Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc became world-famous with Cloudy Bay's ____ vintage.
steps.explanation: Cloudy Bay's 1985 launched the Marlborough style.

steps.title: Variations
steps.body: Marlborough isn't one style. The Wairau Valley gives classic tropical, aromatic wines; the Awatere Valley, cooler and windier, gives more herbal, mineral, saline wines. Some producers use barrel fermentation, wild yeast or lees ageing for more complex, textured versions.

steps.explanation: Most Marlborough Sauvignon is unoaked and fresh.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Marlborough's sun and cold nights give intense, fresh Sauvignon
The Awatere gives a cooler, more herbal style
